notes: The as well ... as pair is not rule 14's correlative given to one connective: two comparative כְּ morphemes stand in the Hebrew, so each takes only the English written for it, and rule 24 heads the first on as rather than on well.
The italic of Jehovah in the closing clause is added; the Hebrew there writes only שֵׁם, and no morpheme licenses the repeated genitive (rules 7, 30).
Both cognate infinitives absolute take their distinct intensifiers (surely, certainly) under rule 56, the finite verbs keeping their subjects and auxiliaries.
אֶזְרָח is headed on home under rule 31's subtraction; heading on born was the competing reading.
